chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from Jamīl, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Concerning one who does not know whether he has prayed three or four, and his uncertainty regarding that is equal, he said: He said, «When the uncertainty is evenly balanced between three and four, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he may pray one rakʿah while standing, and if he wishes, he may pray two rakʿahs and four sajdahs.»
ai.seo_question: What should someone do in salat (prayer) if they are equally unsure whether they prayed three or four rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person who becomes equally uncertain in salat (prayer) whether he has prayed three rakʿahs or four. In such a case, he is given the choice between performing one rakʿah standing or two rakʿahs with four sajdahs as the corrective prayer.
